newsitem.title: USA: CalPERS says will continue pressure on ADM.
newsitem.headline: CalPERS says will continue pressure on ADM.

text.p: California Public Employees' Retirement System (CalPERS) said Thursday it will continue to meet with Archer Daniels Midland Co to make the agribusiness giant more responsive to shareholders.

"CalPERS will continue to meet with directors and pursue the wishes of shareholders that want a majority of independent directors and increased oversight of the ADM Board," said Charles Valdes, chairman of CalPERS investment committee, in a statement.
"Our campaign to gain true independence won't stop until ADM has a fully independent board that makes clear and objective decisions in the best long term interests of shareholders," he said.

Earlier Thursday, a proposal requiring a majority of independent directors on the board was defeated at the company's annual shareholders meeting held in Decatur, Ill., but received 42 percent of the votes cast.
Other shareholder proposals addressing corporate governance issues did not pass. ADM's slate of 12 directors was approved by about 89 percent, the company announced at the meeting.

"Today's vote is a clear victory for CalPERS and all institutional investors. Forty-two percent of shareholders have expressed their dissatisfaction with the ADM Board of Directors. Given the substantial inside ownership of the company, this vote sends a powerful message to the ADM Board that shareholders want change," Valdes said.
